pronunciation.t: ع (ayn) is a deep throaty sound
pronunciation.tip: Tighten your throat like swallowing in reverse: عَرب (ʿarab) = Arab.

pronunciation.t: ح (ḥa) is a breathy deep H
pronunciation.tip: Breathe hard from deep in the throat: حَب (ḥabb) = love.

pronunciation.t: خ (kha) scrapes like clearing your throat
ق (qaf) is a deep K from the back
pronunciation.tip: K made far back in the throat: قَلب (qalb) = heart.

pronunciation.t: ث and ذ are soft TH sounds
pronunciation.tip: ث like THINK (ثلاثة = three), ذ like THIS (ذهب = gold).

alphabet.title: The Arabic alphabet
alphabet.explain: Arabic has 28 letters, written right-to-left. Letters change shape at the start, middle and end of words — but the sounds stay the same. Learn sounds first, shapes second!

counting.title: Counting 0 to 100
counting.explain: Numbers 1–10 first, then 11–19 (ones + عشر), then tens to 100. 21 = واحد وعشرون (one and twenty) — ones come FIRST!
rules: 21+ puts ones FIRST: واحد وعشرون = 21 (one-and-twenty). Tens end in -ون: عشرون، ثلاثون.

level.title: Starter: greetings, gender, first verbs

lessons.title: Greetings: السلام عليكم
lessons.learn: The famous greeting! السلام عليكم (peace upon you) → answer وعليكم السلام (and upon you peace). Morning: صباح الخير → answer صباح النور! Greetings always come in PAIRS.

grammar.title: Greetings come in pairs
grammar.explain: السلام عليكم → وعليكم السلام. صباح الخير → صباح النور (morning of light!). مساء الخير → مساء النور. Never answer a greeting with the same greeting — use its PAIR!
mistakes: Answering السلام عليكم with السلام عليكم — reply وعليكم السلام!
Saying صباح الخير at night — evenings need مساء الخير!

dialogue.en: And upon you peace! Good morning!

lessons.title: Names and how are you
lessons.learn: اسمي ليلى = My name is Layla. Ask: ما اسمك؟ (m) / ما اسمكِ؟ (f) — -KA for men, -KI for women! How are you: كيف حالك؟ → بخير، الحمد لله (fine, praise God)!

grammar.title: -ka (m) / -ki (f): your
grammar.explain: اسمكَ (ismuka) = your name (to a man), اسمكِ (ismukī) = your name (to a woman). حالكَ/حالكِ the same. اسمي = MY name (works for everyone). Check who you talk to — pick -KA or -KI!
mistakes: Saying اسمك to a woman — women get اسمكِ (-KI)!
Forgetting الحمد لله after بخير — it always follows!

dialogue.en: My name is Layla. What is yours? (to m)

lessons.title: Gender: هذا / هذه
lessons.learn: Two genders! هذا = this (m), هذه = this (f). Feminine usually ends in ة (ta marbuta): مدرسة (school-f), سيارة (car-f). No ة? Usually masculine: كتاب (book-m), بيت (house-m)!

grammar.title: هذا (m) / هذه (f) + ة
grammar.explain: هذا كتاب (this is a book-m), هذه مدرسة (this is a school-f). Adjectives match: رجل كبير (big man), امرأة كبيرة (big woman) — feminine adds ة!
mistakes: Saying هذا مدرسة — ة-words need هذه!
Saying امرأة كبير — feminine needs كبيرة!

dialogue.en: Yes, this is a big book.
Yes! This is a small school.

lessons.title: Plurals: كتاب → كتب
lessons.learn: Plurals transform! Sound feminine: سيارة → سيارات (add -ات). People masculine: مدرس → مدرسون (-ون). And BROKEN plurals reshape the word: كتاب → كتب, قلم → أقلام. Learn each word WITH its plural!

grammar.title: Three plural roads
grammar.explain: سيارة→سيارات (-ات for most feminine). مدرس→مدرسون (-ون for male people). Broken: كتاب→كتب, قلم→أقلام, بيت→بيوت — memorise the pair!
mistakes: Saying كتابات — books are broken: كتب!
Saying مدرسات for male teachers — men take -ون!

lessons.title: Present tense: أنا أدرس
lessons.learn: Verbs wear PREFIXES! أدرس (I study), تدرس (you-m study), يدرس (he studies), تدرس (she studies), ندرس (we study). One verb, five prefixes: أ/ت/ي/ن. Learn the prefix song!

grammar.title: Present prefixes: أ/ت/ي/ن
grammar.explain: أدرس (I study), تدرس (you-m study), يدرس (he studies), تدرس (she studies), ندرس (we study). She and you-m share تـ! Pronouns optional: أدرس alone = I study.
mistakes: Saying أنا يدرس — I takes أدرس!
Adding أنا every time — أدرس alone is enough!

lessons.title: I have: عندي
lessons.learn: عندي = I have (at-me)! عندك (you-m have), عندها (she has). فِي = there is: في البيت (in the house). عندي كتاب = I have a book. Swap endings, own everything!

grammar.title: عندي + thing = I have
grammar.explain: عندي كتاب (I have a book), عندك ماء؟ (do you have water?), ما عندي وقت (I have no time — ما negates!). فِي for places: الكتاب في البيت (the book is in the house).
mistakes: Saying أنا أملك first — natives say عندي!
Saying لا عندي — negate with ما: ما عندي!

dialogue.en: Yes, I have water and bread.
